entities.summary: The Monmouth Railway, also known as the Monmouth Tramroad, was a horse-drawn 3 ft 6 in gauge plateway. It ran for about 5 miles (8.0 km) from Howler's Slade, east of Coleford, in Gloucestershire and Monmouth; there were two branches from other mineral sites. It was intended to bring the mineral products, coal and iron ore, of the Forest of Dean to Monmouth, and to a wharf alongside the River Wye.
